mainEntity.name: Can a loose implant crown be repaired?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, yes. If the abutment screw has simply loosened, a dental professional can access the screw, re-torque it to the correct specification, and reseal the access channel. If the crown itself is cement-retained and the cement has failed, the crown may be recemented. However, the appropriate course of action depends on a full clinical assessment of the implant and its components. Treatment suitability always depends on individual circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How long should a dental implant crown last?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universally guaranteed lifespan for an implant crown, as longevity depends on many factors including the quality of the original placement, the patient's oral hygiene, bite forces, and whether any complications arise. With appropriate care and maintenance, implant crowns can function well for many years, and the implant fixture itself may last considerably longer. Individual outcomes vary and cannot be predicted with certainty without a clinical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for an implant crown to feel slightly different after placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: A period of adjustment is not uncommon after a new implant crown is fitted, as the mouth adapts to the new restoration. However, if the crown feels obviously loose, uncomfortable, or the bite feels persistently uneven, this should be reported to the dental practice promptly for assessment and any necessary adjustment.

mainEntity.name: Does grinding teeth affect dental implants differently from natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Natural teeth are suspended in the jawbone by the periodontal ligament, which acts as a shock absorber and provides a degree of flexibility under biting forces. Dental implants are anchored directly to the bone without this ligament, meaning they do not have the same natural cushioning. This makes implants potentially more susceptible to the effects of bruxism, which is why managing grinding habits is particularly important for implant patients.

mainEntity.name: How often should I have my dental implant checked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most dental professionals recommend check-ups at least once or twice a year for implant patients, though individual recommendations may vary based on oral health status and risk factors. Your dental professional will advise on the most appropriate maintenance schedule for your specific situation. Consistent attendance at these appointments helps detect any changes early.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if my implant crown falls off?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your implant crown detaches, keep it safe and contact your dental practice as soon as possible to arrange an assessment. Avoid attempting to reattach it yourself. The implant fixture itself is typically still present in the jawbone, and prompt professional assessment will determine the cause of the detachment and the appropriate course of management. In most cases, this is not an emergency, but timely attention is advisable.
